title: A spiropyran–pyridinium fluorophore for light-gated dual monitoring of HOCl and SO 2  in mitochondria
content: Monitoring of multiple analytes together, such as hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and sulfur dioxide (SO2), through their corresponding aqueous species, ClO− and sulfite, respectively, is important for gaining deeper insight into complex cellular processes. Fluorescent molecular probes capable of dual-channel responses provide a powerful approach for tracking such species within subcellular environments. Here, we report a spiropyran–pyridinium conjugate, SPI-PYD, designed for the dual-channel sequential detection of ClO− and SO32− in the mitochondrial microenvironment. The probe exhibits distinct fluorescence responses governed by chemical reactions with the analytes and photoinduced switching. Reaction with ClO− produces enhanced green fluorescence, whereas UV irradiation induces spiropyran-to-merocyanine switching, enabling efficient FRET, resulting in strong red emission. Subsequent reaction with SO32− perturbs this FRET state, leading to a decrease in red-channel emission accompanied by an increase in green fluorescence. These light-gated sequential changes in the green and red emission channels enable ratiometric discrimination of ClO− and SO32−. SPI-PYD exhibits excellent mitochondrial localization, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.85, along with good aqueous solubility and low cytotoxicity. Fluorescence imaging in SK-BR-3 breast cancer cells further demonstrates the intracellular ratiometric sensing capability of SPI-PYD toward ClO− and SO32−. Given the important roles of these species in mitochondrial redox homeostasis and cellular stress responses, their dynamic monitoring at the organelle level could provide valuable insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying mitochondrial dysfunction and stress-associated cellular processes.
